bullets.text: Update every import and call site (19 files)

behaviour.instructions: Does this change alter runtime behaviour (not just names, formatting, comments or types)?

breaking.instructions: Would existing code or clients that use what this unit itself defines stop compiling or behave wrongly if they were not updated (an export removed or renamed, a parameter added without a default, a return type or response field changed or removed, stricter validation)?

criteria.false: additions only (a new export, a new optional parameter or field), internal code, a call site or import updated to follow a change made elsewhere, a test, or code moved without changing its interface
criteria.true: this unit changes an exported function, type, endpoint, schema or setting in a way its existing users must adapt to

contract.instructions: Which interface that other code or clients rely on does this unit itself define or change? Most units change none: implementation inside a function, call sites and imports that follow a change made elsewhere, UI rendering, tests and moved code are none.

criteria.api shape: the route, method, request or response fields of an HTTP or RPC endpoint served or called over the network
criteria.env/flag: an environment variable, config key or feature flag that is read or introduced
criteria.event format: the shape of an emitted event, message or log line consumed elsewhere
criteria.none: no interface change: internal logic, call sites or imports updated to follow another change, UI markup, tests, comments, or code moved without changing its interface
criteria.schema/migration: a database table, column or index, or a data migration
criteria.signature: the name, parameters or return type of an exported function, method, type or component that other modules import

covered.instructions: Is this change exercised by any of the test files changed in this pull request (listed in the state)?

depth.instructions: How closely does a reviewer need to look at this change?

criteria.read: needs a careful line-by-line read: new or changed logic, state, error handling, concurrency, security or data handling
criteria.run locally: needs to be run or tested by hand to be sure: behaviour, timing or environment effects that reading alone cannot settle
criteria.skim: a glance is enough: imports, exports, type declarations, wiring, renames, call sites updated to follow another change, simple markup, tests
criteria.skip: nothing to review: generated output, formatting, comments, or code moved unchanged

desc_bullet.instructions: Which bullet of the pull request description does this change implement?

criteria.b2: Update every import and call site (19 files)
criteria.none: implements none of the listed bullets

effect.instructions: Where would a user or client first notice the effect of this change?

criteria.api response: the shape or content of an API response
criteria.stored data: what is written to a database, file or cache
criteria.ui: what the user interface shows or how it behaves

fail_mode.instructions: If this change is wrong, what is the most likely kind of failure?

criteria.cosmetic: a visual or textual glitch only
criteria.crash: an exception, panic or failed request
criteria.wrong data: silently incorrect results or corrupted data

kind.instructions: What kind of change is this unit, judged by its main purpose?

criteria.config: changes configuration, build, CI or environment settings
criteria.dependency: adds, removes or bumps a dependency or lockfile entry
criteria.feature: adds or extends user-visible or API-visible functionality
criteria.formatting: whitespace, ordering or style only; no change in meaning
criteria.generated: machine-generated output such as codegen, snapshots or vendored files
criteria.perf: makes existing behaviour faster or cheaper
criteria.refactor: restructures code without changing what it does
criteria.test: adds or changes tests or test helpers

relevance.instructions: How relevant is this change to the reviewer, given their role and the paths they own (listed in the state)?
criteria: 1: unrelated to their role and paths

reversible.instructions: Could this change be reverted with a plain code revert, without a migration or a data fix?

risk.instructions: How bad would it be if this change were wrong?
criteria: 2: low, a minor annoyance that is easy to fix
3: moderate, a visible bug for some users
4: high, broken core flow or wrong data
5: severe, outage, data loss or security hole
